goal: Archive terminal specs, the last unfinished part of the 2026-08-20-003 roadmap item. docs/specs/ still holds 206 active specs against 82 archived, unchanged by that slice. A spec counts as terminal when a Plan under docs/plans/archive/ implements it, established by either of two signals: the archived Plan's normalized filename matches the spec's, or the archived Plan cites the spec's docs/specs/<name>.spec.md path in its text. Neither signal alone suffices -- measured today filename matching resolves 113 and text citation 117, but their union resolves 150 of 206 because only 105 of 244 archived Plans cite a spec path at all. Whatever the union leaves undetermined must be listed explicitly in the slice output and left in place, never archived on a guess. That mirrors the two-signal-then-enumerate rule already used for intent sidecars. Run this after 2026-08-20-005. That slice archives 29 prose Plans, which converts their spec linkages from active to archived and shrinks the undetermined set before this slice measures it; several currently undetermined specs such as 2026-08-05-risk-tiered-workflow-execution resolve for exactly that reason. Archival is a move into docs/specs/archive/, never a delete. Two exposures are known. tests/python-reference-boundary.test.ts pins the active path docs/specs/opencode-native-plugin.spec.md and must be reconciled if that spec is archived. Cross-document links across a 206-file corpus are the larger one, which is why both link scripts are in scope. Do not touch the instructional-reference exemption list that 2026-08-20-003 established; specs citing retired tools as the subject of retirement stay active and exempt.

acceptance.assertion: Every spec resolved terminal by either linkage signal lives under docs/specs/archive/, each move preserves content and none was deleted, and specs left undetermined by both signals remain in docs/specs/ and are enumerated explicitly rather than archived on a guess.
